subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia and rare gynaecological cancers

steps.tx: **Complete hydatidiform moles** are diploid, androgenetic 46,XX or 46,XY conceptuses lacking embryonic fetal tissue, carrying a 15% to 20% risk of malignant gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. They result from fertilization of an enucleated ovum by a single sperm that duplicates its genome or by dispermy. In contrast, partial moles are triploid 69,XXX or 69,XXY gestations containing fetal parts with under five percent malignant transformation risk.

points: Diffuse hydropic villi, severe trophoblast hyperplasia

right.title: Partial Hydatidiform Mole

steps.tx: The section shows **complete hydatidiform mole** with swollen **hydropic villi** holding central cisterns and rimmed by circumferential **trophoblast hyperplasia**. No fetal tissue is present, matching a diploid androgenetic conceptus. Spotting this diffuse pattern matters because complete moles carry substantial risk of later neoplasia and require close hormone surveillance after evacuation.
steps.say: This histology shows a complete hydatidiform mole with diffusely swollen villi, clear central cisterns, and circumferential trophoblast proliferation without fetal tissue. The lesson describes this as a diploid androgenetic conceptus with a meaningful risk of later gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Recognizing the pattern explains why careful evacuation and prolonged hormone follow up are required.

vis.caption: Complete mole shows hydropic villi with trophoblast hyperplasia. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Serial quantitative serum human chorionic gonadotropin monitoring is mandatory following uterine evacuation of a molar pregnancy. **Post-molar GTN** is diagnosed by serum beta-hCG plateaus over 4 consecutive values across 3 weeks, consecutive rises over 2 weeks, or histological choriocarcinoma. Persistently elevated hCG beyond six months post-evacuation also establishes the diagnosis, requiring formal anatomical staging and risk scoring.

nodes.label: Plateau (4 values / 3 wks) or Rise (3 values / 2 wks)

steps.tx: Anatomical staging is integrated with prognostic risk factors to guide therapy. The **FIGO/WHO** prognostic scoring system stratifies GTN into low-risk score 0 to 6 managed with single-agent chemotherapy and high-risk score 7 or higher requiring combination regimens. Variables scored from zero to four include age, antecedent pregnancy type, interval from pregnancy, baseline hCG, tumour size, metastatic sites, and prior failed chemotherapy.

rows: Induction EP followed by EMA-CO / surgical resection

steps.tx: **Low-risk gestational** trophoblastic neoplasia is treated with single-agent intramuscular methotrexate with folinic acid rescue or pulsed intravenous actinomycin D. The standard eight-day methotrexate regimen delivers 1 mg/kg on days 1, 3, 5, and 7, accompanied by folinic acid 0.1 mg/kg on days 2, 4, 6, and 8 every 2 weeks. Consolidation therapy is continued for two to three cycles past the first normal hCG reading.

steps.tx: High-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is treated with multi-agent **EMA-CO** etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D, cyclophosphamide, and vincristine, curing over 90% of patients. EMA-CO is administered on days 1, 2, and 8 every 2 weeks. In patients with massive tumour burden, low-dose induction etoposide and cisplatin avoids massive acute tumour lysis or fatal haemorrhage before initiating full EMA-CO.

steps.tx: **Placental site trophoblastic** tumour PSTT arises from intermediate trophoblast, secretes human placental lactogen hPL with low beta-hCG, and is relatively chemoresistant requiring hysterectomy. Unlike syncytiotrophoblastic choriocarcinomas, PSTT grows slowly, invades myometrium deeply, and metastasizes late. If disease spreads beyond the pelvis, intensive platinum-etoposide regimens like EP-EMA are required.

right.title: Placental Site Trophoblastic Tumour
points: Low beta-hCG, elevated hPL and CD146

steps.tx: The section shows broad **sheets of intermediate trophoblast** pushing deep between muscle fibres, marking **deep myometrial invasion**. Stains show diffuse strong **human placental lactogen** with only focal **beta hCG**, the classic PSTT profile. This pattern matters because these tumours resist standard single agent chemotherapy, so confined disease is managed by hysterectomy rather than drugs alone.
steps.say: This is placental site trophoblastic tumour. Sheets of intermediate trophoblast invade deeply into the uterine muscle. Staining is strongly positive for human placental lactogen but only focal for beta hCG. Unlike choriocarcinoma, this entity grows slowly, responds poorly to chemotherapy and usually needs hysterectomy when still confined to the uterus.

vis.alt: Histology shows intermediate trophoblast invading uterine muscle with strong hPL and focal beta hCG staining.
vis.caption: Trophoblast invasion with classic staining supports hysterectomy. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Invasive **vulvar squamous cell** carcinoma spreading to regional groin lymph nodes mandates inguinal femoral lymphadenectomy or sentinel node biopsy for depth over 1 mm. Unilateral or bilateral lymphadenectomy is performed depending on primary tumour distance from midline. Ipsilateral inguinal lymph node involvement serves as the strongest predictor of disease-specific mortality, indicating adjuvant pelvic and groin radiotherapy.

steps.tx: Malignant **ovarian germ cell** tumours dysgerminoma, endodermal sinus tumour are exquisitely chemosensitive, curable with fertility-sparing surgery and BEP chemotherapy. Regimens combine bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin for three to four cycles. Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with preservation of the contralateral ovary and uterus is standard even in advanced stages, safely retaining endocrine and reproductive potential.
